card.title: THE REGULARS
card.text: Becomes Veteran when it is fully repaired.
card.flavorText: The 6th Infantry Regiment, nicknamed “Regulars”, is a regiment of the US Army which has been active from 1812 to present day. During WWII, the regiment was a unit of the 1st Armored Division which played a significant role as one of the first American units to cross the Atlantic and engage the Axis powers. Departing from Fort Dix, New Jersey on April 11, 1942, they arrived in Northern Ireland on May 16, 1942. Intensively trained, they prepared for their first combat which was Operation Torch, the seaborne invasion of French North Africa. The 6th Armored Infantry Regiment, commanded by Colonel Claud E. Stadtman, faced challenges during this operation. While one battalion suffered heavy casualties in the assault on Oran, another battalion successfully captured the Tafaraoui airfield. Despite setbacks, the overall objective was achieved. The regiment then moved to Tunisia, where they confronted a German-Italian counterattack. In December 1942, the 1st and 2nd Battalions of the 6th Armored Infantry bravely defended a critical defensive line against heavy enemy fire. They held their positions, contributing to the broader Allied effort. Subsequently, in October 1943, the regiment landed in Italy. Eventually, it underwent reorganization, with its elements being redesignated as parts of the 1st Armored Division.
